      price-sensitive SMB accounts

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale:
The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, which rules out the most tempting response to the competitor. memory_73 is the only inherited record with a quantified downside (signups +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%, weak renewals): promotional pricing buys top-line motion by importing churn-prone accounts, and matching an entry-price competitor in the same price-sensitive SMB segment would repeat that at worse terms. Referral incentive (memory_57) is real but addresses established customers, not the two metrics actually deteriorating. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is sound but does not touch a 6% activation or 4% onboarding decline.

That leaves the two funnel levers. Onboarding completion is plausibly upstream of the activation drop, so memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) is the higher-leverage intervention, with memory_91 as the fallback if verification weakens it. I am spending both verification pulls on the two memories I would actually act on rather than on memory_73, whose downside is already quantified and does not need re-checking.

What I want from the archive: (1) whether memory_86's lift was measured on completion rate alone or carried through to retained, paying, qualified accounts — completion is a proxy that can be inflated by removing steps that establish value; (2) the baseline period and segment mix, since both records predate the current competitive environment and a lift measured in a calmer quarter may not transfer.

Downstream value risk, explicitly: memory_31 achieved its lift by cutting required signup fields. Those fields are the qualification and routing data that memory_44 depends on to push enterprise prospects into the demo-request path. If 'simplify onboarding' is implemented as field removal, the measured win (faster activation) can be paid for with an unmeasured loss (worse lead quality, enterprise prospects misrouted into self-serve) — activation improves while qualified revenue degrades. So I scope this to post-signup step reduction, not signup field removal, and I hold qualification fields intact.

Scale: standard experiment, not broad rollout, because the inherited effects are stale relative to current conditions. Guardrails beyond completion rate: week-four retention, qualified-pipeline rate per signup, and enterprise routing share, with a pre-committed rollback if qualified pipeline per signup falls even as completion rises. If verification shows memory_86 measured only completion with no revenue-side follow-through, I switch to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger decline and carries no lead-quality exposure.
